title: Helpful Tips and Exercises for Increased Back Health and Comfort
text: Since most humans will experience some back pain in their lives it is important to know how to prevent it. However when the author states that back pain is "not a very serious condition," she has perhaps never been immobilized to the point of hardly being able to walk for a week.Needless to say, this author does provide information on anatomy that is interesting. She gives a list of reasons why your back can get injured (picking up a heavy object or case of water bottles for instance) but in my reality even sitting for too long in a comfortable office chair is enough to make me stiff and cause back pain. So I avoid sitting in the office too long and don't read books on the computer. This book does mention the problem of being deskbound as a cause for back pain and I'd agree it is very true.You will find this book has a lot of useful information to encourage a more comfortable life experience. Jennifer King describes stretches and exercises to increase back health. I also found her tips on how to perform normal activities (brushing your teeth can become a challenge when your back is out) more safely were very useful and do work.This book is worth reading for the many interesting ideas and wise advice. There is nothing too complicated in this book so I'd say this is appropriate for those who struggle with back pain now and then. Of course you should consult with your doctor before taking any advice in this book.~The Rebecca Review

title: Picture quality is great, but causes an echo during videoconferences.
text: I've had this camera a few months. The install went pretty well. I had to reboot a few times to pick the camera up, but once it was recognized, that has worked well. The camera does not clamp securely onto my external monitor. I fixed that problem by getting a separate flexible arm that clamps onto my desk and holds the camara. I love the physical lens cover so I can easily control when the camera is capturing an image. The picture quality is great. I love having an external camera instead of relying on the one on my laptop so my laptop can stay connected to the docking station and I don't have to try to get it moved over to the center of my desk every time I have a videoconference. Unfortnately there there are two remaining problems that are making me now decide to look for another camera:1. Echos: When using this camera, is it causes an echo on videoconferencing that others can hear. I cannot hear it. It is so annoying to others that immediately people start talking about it and asking if the call can be done using some other audio. It definitely happens on Microsoft Teams calls as others have said in the Questions section for this product on Amazon. I can't remember if it happened on Webex videocalls also. Others have said switching the audio source solves that problem.2. Wide View: This may be standard on these cameras. I'll find out when I shop for a new one, but the view is much wider than my native laptop camera. I can't find any way on the camera to "crop" it so that it shows only the person during videoconference and not a lot of what is to the right and left of the person. I solved that problem by installing OBS Studio and the OBS virtual camera. OBS allows me to crop the picture and then uses that video as the "camera" in Microsoft Teams. That works very well to get a good cropped video, however, the image quality went way down and it freezes up sometimes, so it is not a great solution because I end up not having smooth starts to videoconferences with all the troubleshooting I have to do to get OBS, the webcam, and the conferecing software to all work together.I hope I can find a camera that works seemlessly so that the now much more frequent videoconferences, thanks to the pandemic, will go more smoothly.

title: My favorite mascara at a reasonable price
text: I know a lot of us spend a small fortune on beauty products, but if I find a product that works for me at a “drug store price,” I’m going to stay with it.My daughter once recommended this Maybelline mascara because I was having trouble finding one with an applicator I liked. This product comes with a silicone applicator called a “grabber” with the rounded shape being very narrow at the tip but wider at the base. It really helps me apply just the amount of mascara I want and separate the lashes that might stick together.I use the brownish black color and apply my first coat carefully…not too much, not too little. I’m not trying to build up my lashes unnaturally but trying to separate and lengthen them. (I am not a fan of the fiber mascara for myself.)I may apply a second coat but try not to wait too long. For me, the dryer everything gets, the more clumpy my lashes might look.If my mascara starts going on in clumps, I know it’s time to switch to a new tube. I always have back-ups ready to go.I learned long ago not to pump the brush in and out of the tube…this just adds air and causes the product to dry out faster. I just twist it gently in the tube to get it on the brush.Before my mascara dries, I use a small coarse brush (you can buy them in packs) to better separate the eyelashes and get them going in the right direction.If I accidentally get any on the skin under my eyes, a Q-tip works well to wisk it off.I never see flecks of mascara on my face. It lasts all day unless, of course, I rub my eyes…which I don’t really do.I remove the product at night with Neutrogena eye make-up remover which works well for me and is gentle on my skin.I am totally happy with this mascara (and frankly love the pink and green color of the tube). The wand is easy for me to hold and control, versus some of those thicker tubes.I highly recommend (we each really have to find what works best for us) and will continue to purchase. I find it a great value.

I like Cyn. Honestly, I’m animal obsessed so she was sure to be likable to me. She’s also a very hard worker who has dealt with a lot of sadness in her life, but has preserved in spite of it. I just like her personality, I would want to be friends with her.Cameron as a hero is very likable. He’s a really good brother, to what can only be described as a complicated family life. His dad apparently really enjoys getting married and divorced resulting in a heck of a lot of siblings. He’s a smart guy, who is good at his job, but is under a lot of stress. It totally understandable while being someone other than himself would be enjoyable for him. But even he knows its not the best idea.Part of what makes this book so enjoyable is the situations these two’s families manage to get themselves into, but our couple in question is probably the most down to earth of the bunch. I really liked their respective mothers, the sibling relationships, and the wide variety of animals that make an appearance in the book. This is not a book that’s heavy on the heat, but more lighthearted and emotional connection. It was a quick fun read for me.

title: Be careful putting it on....
text: I the end, I gave 5 stars because of good customer service. I initially had trouble finding a case that I liked and that seemed worth the money for my new S21 5G. There just weren't a lot of choices. Then I saw this one. I like this color - not too flashy, but something different besides plain black or white. The price was pretty good, so I figured it was no huge loss if I changed to another later.It was a bit difficult to put on. Like many more durable cases, it has the inner hard plastic shell and a second outer layer that is softer and more grippable. The inner hard plastic shell broke at the top when I was trying to put it on. I still managed to put it on and the outer shell held it all together pretty well despite the break. I was still a little annoyed, so I messaged the company telling them that it broke while I was trying to put it on - and they promptly sent me a brand new one, no return required, no hassle at all.All in all, pretty pleased. I would say to be careful when putting the case on. But once it's on, it feels quite sturdy. It has the "lip" to keep your screen from smashing into the ground if you drop it, too. My popsocket sticks to it fine. All the button markers and holes are in the right place. And the customer service is top notch. It's not an expensive case like otterbox, but the feel of the case reminds me of otterbox cases I had on previous phones. I was rather surprised at how sturdy it felt once on my phone, especially given the price.So.Pros:* Cheap price* Looks good* Feels very sturdy with the inner and outer layers* "Lip" to keep screen from getting smashed if you drop your phone on a flat surface* Great customer service if you have a problemCons:* A little bit of a struggle to get on for me* The hard plastic inner shell will snap at a thin part if not careful when applying force, but the company seems to replace for free with no hassle if this happens.
